text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chretien stirs Phillipine issue: Remark favouring return of Ramos as president ignites controversy on trade trip.
- Cold hits domestic supplies of gas: Heating bills soar for Canadians.
- Mideast peace process renewed: Compromise pact signals progress.
- Universe will end, but no time soon: U.S. scientists set out cosmic calendar.
- Transit costs unloaded on Ontario cities, towns: Islander heckle minister throughout announcement.
- Dollar jumps half a cent: Bullish economic review in prestigious London paper, forecasts of stable U.S. rates cited.
- Robert Friedland plans to sue U.S.: Justice Department drops bid to freeze assets.
- Timbuktu says it won't recoup Reese advance: C$2.3 million sent to U.S. firm controlled by former president.
- Microsoft rolls out Office 97: But windows 95 hype won't accompany software suite.
- Chill winds blowing toward Bay Street: When the market cool, stock traders face being reined in. There are concerns over the risks they are taking.
- Banks bow to shareholders: Proposals to limit executive pay and selection of board members must be put to shareholders by Royal Bank and National Bank after they lose appeal of Quebec court ruling.
